description:
In the Muslim Town locality near Ichhra, within a graveyard that still bears his name and lends it to a surrounding housing scheme, lies the tomb of Hazrat Baba Shah Kamal, remembered chiefly as the elder brother of the celebrated Sufi Baba Shah Jamal. Their father, Syed Ahmad Shah, a descendant of Jalaluddin Surkh-Posh Bukhari of Uch Sharif, personally instructed both sons in Islamic theology before the brothers settled together in the Ichhra area of Lahore. While far less is independently documented about Shah Kamal than about his more famous sibling, local devotional tradition attaches to him the composite title "Qadiri Suhrawardi," suggesting an affiliation with the same overlapping Sufi orders associated with his brother's shrine nearby, and his likely lifetime is generally placed in the same late-sixteenth to seventeenth-century Mughal-era window as Shah Jamal's own. The shrine sits within the historic Shah Kamal graveyard, still in active use as a burial ground, and continues to attract local devotees for weekly Thursday evening gatherings involving dhol drumming and qawwali, echoing in more modest form the famous dhamal tradition at his brother's shrine. An annual urs is held in his honour, drawing pilgrims from the surrounding neighbourhoods, though the precise calendar date is not widely documented. The site is formally catalogued as a monument of the historic period by the Punjab Department of Archaeology and Museums, and together with the Shah Jamal shrine it helps anchor the religious identity of this part of Lahore as a historic centre of Sufi devotion, reflecting the broader pattern by which entire Lahore neighbourhoods have taken their names and characters from the saints buried within them. This location is independently confirmed by two directly-consulted sources: the Punjab Auqaf & Religious Affairs Department's own shrine listing includes, under its Lahore Zone, an entry titled "Darbar & Jamia Masjid Hazrat Shah Kamal," while the Chughtai Library's digital catalogue of Lahore's historic Mughal-period monuments gives the shrine's precise address as Karnalpura, Muslim Town, Combo Colony, Lahore, and records it as owned by the Auqaf Department, its condition rated "Satisfactory," within a mosque-and-graveyard complex.

## Bibliography
- Auqaf & Religious Affairs Department, Government of Punjab, "Shrines" (official shrine listing), https://auqaf.punjab.gov.pk/shrines, accessed 16 August 2026.
- Chughtai (Public) Library Digital Library, "Historic Monuments of Lahore — Mughal Period — Shrine of Hazrat Shah Kamal," https://www.chughtailibrary.com/digital_library/place_detail.php?plc_id=35, accessed 16 August 2026.
qa_note: A travel-content site (beautyofpakistan.com — excluded from this archive's citation standard as a travel aggregator) describes a "Shrine of Baba Kamal Chishti" on a hilltop on Ferozepur Road in Kasur, distinct in nisba (Chishti, versus the Suhrawardi/"Qadiri Suhrawardi" affiliation used for the saint in this entry) and in site type (hilltop shrine versus urban Ichhra tomb) from the shrine described here. This may simply be a different, unrelated saint who happens to share a similar name, rather than a rival claim about the same shrine — flagged here for awareness, not resolved, and not treated as a verified source.
